history.period: 1758 AD (one source says 1759 - minor conflict, verify)
history.summary: CSV CORRECTION: 'Radha Shyam Temple, Bishnupur, Manipur' is documented as the Radha Shyam Temple at Bishnupur, BANKURA district, WEST BENGAL - the CSV's state (Manipur) is wrong; this is the well-known 18th-century Malla temple, not a Manipur shrine. (A tourmyindia page titled 'Radha Shyam Temple Bishnupur, Manipur' reproduces the Bankura temple's details under a Manipur URL path - a documented aggregator conflation.) Built in 1758 (chitrolekha.com says 1759) by Malla King Chaitanya Singha, it is the youngest of the major Malla temples. Square on plan (11 m base, 9.2 m height), south-facing, it is an eka-ratna (single-spire) laterite temple whose cylindrical shikhara carries a semi-spherical dome - a form some writers trace to Muslim/Mughal architectural influence. The outer walls carry fine low-relief stucco work with geometric, floral, epic and Puranic motifs. It is a living temple, and images from dilapidated temples of the locality are housed in its sanctum; maintained by the Archaeological Survey of India.

name: Radha Shyam Temple
town_description: Bishnupur in Bankura district, West Bengal, was the capital of the Malla dynasty from the 8th century and is famous as Bengal's terracotta temple town - Rasmancha (c.1600), Jor Bangla (1655), Shyam Rai/Pancharatna (1643), Madan Mohan and others. The town is also home to the Bishnupur Gharana of Hindustani classical music, Baluchari silk weaving, and the famous Bankura terracotta horse. Not to be confused with Bishnupur, Manipur.
tradition: Vaishnavism (Gaudiya Vaishnavism; dedicated to Radha and Krishna)
